description: Sync the files inside the Dropbox folders you choose, one document per file. With Enforce ACL on, the members of each file's shared folder decide who can find it.
opening: Sync the files inside the Dropbox folders you select, and in every folder below them. Each file is one document. Files are downloaded and their text is read. A file whose text cannot be read is still findable by its path, size and modified time.

With Enforce ACL on, a file can be read only by the members of the shared folder that holds it, or only by the connecting member for files in their own unshared space. Sharing set on a single file is not read. The first sync reaches only files modified in the last 30 days unless you raise `lookback_days`. Files deleted in Dropbox stay in HydraDB, and no author or owner is recorded.

permissions.who_can_read: Each file follows the shared folder that contains it. The folder's members and invitees can read it, and so can members of a group the folder is shared with. A file in the connecting member's own unshared space can be read by that member only.
permissions.identity: A member's or invitee's email address. A group is turned into its members' email addresses when the Dropbox Business team scopes are granted.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a shared folder's members, or cannot turn a group into its members, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: Sharing set on an individual file, rather than on its shared folder, is not read.
Without `sharing.read`, shared folder members can be unreadable.
Without the Business team scopes, a folder shared with a group cannot be fully resolved.
A very large folder or group membership list that cannot be read in full counts as unreadable.
When a shared folder's members change, a later sync applies the new access to its files, including files that did not change.

connect.auth: Dropbox uses an app you create in Dropbox, authorized for offline access: an app key, an app secret and a refresh token.

credentials.name: refresh_token
credentials.text: A long-lived offline refresh token for the connecting account.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes to give the Dropbox app

permissions.name: account_info.read
permissions.text: required. Identifies the account and whether it is a Business account. Without it, team folders are never picked up.

permissions.name: files.metadata.read
permissions.text: required. Sees folders, files and what changed.

permissions.name: files.content.read
permissions.text: required. Reads file contents. Without it, only name, location and size are known.

permissions.name: sharing.read
permissions.text: required. Sees who each folder is shared with, which decides who can find its files.

permissions.name: team_info.read
permissions.text: optional, Business only. Tells that the connection is to a team.

permissions.name: team_data.member
permissions.text: optional, Business only. Reads the team's files on behalf of the member who connected.

permissions.name: groups.read
permissions.text: optional, Business only. Reads group members, so a folder shared with a group resolves to people.

steps.title: Create a Dropbox app
steps.text: Create a Dropbox app with the four required scopes. For a Dropbox Business team, add the four Business scopes too, so team folders are read and group shares resolve to people.

steps.title: Authorize it offline
steps.text: Authorize the app for offline access with the account to sync, and keep the refresh token.

steps.title: Select folders
steps.text: HydraDB lists your folders by path. Select the folders to sync. Every folder below a selected one is included. To reach files older than 30 days, raise `lookback_days` when you select them.

connect.account: One connector reads one Dropbox account. On a Business team, it reads team files on behalf of the member who connected.

sync.first_sync: Each selected folder reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Files last modified before that window are not synced.
sync.changes: Later syncs pick up the changes Dropbox reports since the last sync. If Dropbox no longer accepts where the last sync stopped, the folder is listed again in full.
sync.edits: An edited file is read again and replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted files are not removed. A file deleted in Dropbox stays searchable in HydraDB.

documents.name: Files
documents.one_document: One Dropbox file. Folders are not documents.
documents.title: The file's path, for example `Projects/Acme/contract.pdf`. A file with no path is titled `Dropbox file` and its id.
documents.text: The file's text when it could be read. Otherwise the title followed by `Path`, `Size` and `Modified` lines. The title is searchable in either case.
documents.date: When the file was last modified on Dropbox's servers.
documents.link_back: Opens the file in the Dropbox web app, at its path.
documents.files: Each file is downloaded and its text is read. Files over 50 MiB keep only their details.

attributes.name: path
attributes.text: The file's path in Dropbox. It is the title, so it is always searchable, and it is the `Path` line when the file's text could not be read.

attributes.name: size
attributes.text: The size in bytes, written as the `Size` line. Searchable only on files whose text could not be read.

attributes.name: server_modified
attributes.text: When the file was last modified on Dropbox's servers. Sets the result date. Written as the `Modified` line, so it is searchable only on files whose text could not be read.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
attributes.text: The path of the folder that directly holds the file, `/` at the top level. Limits a query to the files directly in one folder. Files in its subfolders carry their own folder's path. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
attributes.text: The same folder path. Another way to limit a query to one folder. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's files. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Shared folder members
attributes.text: The email addresses of the members and invitees of the file's shared folder, including members of shared groups. They decide who can read the file when Enforce ACL is on. Not searchable.

attributes.name: rbac_warning
attributes.text: Set when the file's sharing could not be fully resolved. It explains the missing permissions and grants no access.

attributes.name: acl_warning
attributes.text: Set when the sharing of the file's folder could not be read. Explains the failed read.

attributes.name: rev
attributes.text: The Dropbox revision id the document was read from.

attributes.name: dropbox_hash
attributes.text: Dropbox's content hash, for comparing file contents outside HydraDB.

attributes.name: client_modified
attributes.text: The modified time recorded by the app that uploaded the file. The result date uses the server time instead.

example_searches: What does the Acme contract PDF in the Legal folder say about termination?
Which files in the Projects/2026 folder mention the launch date?
When was the pricing spreadsheet last changed?

connections: No links between files, and no links to items in other tools. The folder that holds a file is kept as a filter, not a graph link.
people: No people are attached to files. Dropbox files carry no author or owner in HydraDB.

not_synced: Files last modified before the `lookback_days` window on the first sync.
File comments, version history and Dropbox Paper structure.
Who created or last edited a file.
Sharing set on an individual file.
Deletions: deleted files stay in HydraDB.
